references.text: Moses took Zipporah as his wife and had sons with her, which explains who 'his wife and sons' are in this text.
The names of Moses' sons, Gershom and Eliezer, are mentioned here along with his wife Zipporah.
The staff that Moses took is called 'the staff of God' and is the same staff that was turned into a snake earlier in the chapter.
The staff of God is mentioned again when Moses holds it during the battle against Amalek.
The staff is used to perform signs and wonders in Egypt, including turning the waters of the Nile into blood.
Later, the staff is used to strike the rock to bring forth water, even though Moses was commanded to speak to it.
God commands Moses to take the staff with him to perform the signs, which explains why he took it along.
Jacob and his family also traveled to Egypt, a parallel to Moses' return to Egypt with his family.
Moses takes up the staff of God as an instrument of judgment against Egypt, directly enabling the plagues described later.
The staff that was turned into a snake and back again (4:4) is the same 'staff of God' that Moses takes with him on his journey to Egypt (4:20).
The staff Moses takes with him to Egypt (4:20) is the same one he later uses to strike the Nile and lead the people (17:5).
Moses uses the same staff he took with him to Egypt (4:20) to bring locusts over the land.
